project_type: Sig compiler/toolchain (a Zig 0.17.0 compiler fork; .sig strict mode makes allocator use a compile-time error). Self-hosting: sig builds sig.
build_system: sig_build (zero-allocator build system, @import("sig_build")) driven by build.sig. The compiler binary is src/main.sig. A stage0 `sig` on PATH compiles it. BPF codegen requires the LLVM backend, so the compiler must be built with -Denable-llvm. There is also a cmake path (CMakeLists.txt) and bootstrap.ps1/bootstrap.sh for building the sig_build runner itself.
test_framework: In-file `test "..."` blocks run via the sig compiler; the canonical suite is compiler/test_all.sig wired as the `test` step in build.sig (addTestStep). Unit tests for target/linker logic live alongside the sources in lib/std and src.
build_command: From the worktree root c:\Just-Things\Projects\sb0\sig\.worktrees\sbpf-solana: `sig build -Denable-llvm` (produces a new sig compiler; LLVM needed for BPF codegen). Front-end-only sanity after target-table edits: run the freshly built `sig targets`. The stage0 compiler is C:\Just-Things\Projects\Lib\sig-latest\bin\sig.exe (sig 0.6.0).
test_command: `sig build test` (runs compiler/test_all.sig). For targeted checks, run the specific .sig file's tests with the built compiler. The compiler compiling clean after adding an EhdrMachine/MachineRelocType enum member is itself the primary structural check (every exhaustive switch becomes a compile error until handled).
verification_instructions: 1) After target-table edits (FEAT-002): build with -Denable-llvm, run `sig targets`, confirm the solana os/abi and sbpfv1/2/3 CPUs list, and that `-target sbf-solana-solana` resolves to { .bpfel, .solana, .solana } with default -mcpu sbpfv3. 2) After routing edits: confirm `sig build-lib -dynamic -target sbf-solana-solana` no longer errors TargetCannotDynamicLink or LLD unsupported e_machine 247. 3) After linker edits (FEAT-003): -Denable-llvm must compile with zero switch-exhaustiveness errors; unit-test R_BPF apply and lddw split against PC2 values. 4) After codegen (FEAT-004): llvm-objdump the emitted object, confirm `call imm` == murmur3_32(name) with no residual syscall relocation. 5) FEAT-005: build program.so and byte-verify ELFCLASS64/EI_DATA=1/e_machine=247/e_type/R_BPF relocs/entrypoint dynsym against PC2/PC3; integration deploy under WSL solana-test-validator is the acceptance gate.
snapshot_or_generated_files: lib/std/Target/bpf.sig is auto-generated by tools/update_cpu_features.sig; hand edits there must carry a comment so a future regen preserves them. No other generated files are touched by this task.
environment_constraints: Bootstrap rule: NEVER use upstream zig/forked Solana LLVM to produce the release .so; the Solana toolchain (cargo build-sbf, solana CLI, llvm-readelf/llvm-objdump) is a READ-ONLY reference/measurement + deploy tool, run under WSL, never in the Sig artifact-producing path. The pre-coding captures PC1/PC2/PC3/PC-SYS require WSL + the Solana toolchain. solana-test-validator (acceptance gate) also runs under WSL; if unavailable, byte-level verification is the maximal in-environment proof and the validator run is a documented manual step. Primary dev host is Windows (pwsh). Never cancel running CI workflows.
contribution_requirements: development-hierarchy rule: toolchain changes go in the compiler (lib/std, src/, compiler/, tools/); runtime/library/syscall-wrapper/atomics code belongs in zpm and is OUT of scope. Throwaway test modules go under the worktree .build/sbpf-test/, NEVER in zpm. Read compiler/SB0_ABI_TARGET.md and AGENTS.md before compiler work. Commit locally on branch feat/sbpf-solana; never push. The final merge targets base branch fix/resinator-sig-lib-dir-and-win32-resource.
key_patterns: Target identity is OS+ABI+CPU, not a new arch: the SB0 target keeps aarch64 and distinguishes via os/abi (.sb0), and the Solana target mirrors this by keeping .bpfel and distinguishing via os/abi (.solana) + CPU sbpfv3. The precedent for adding a custom OS/ABI is the existing `.sb0` arms in lib/std/Target.sig at lines 162, 403, 844, 1091 (object-format override), 2335, 2501, 2942, 3251, plus the Os.Tag/Abi enum members and isSb0 (~2251). Elf2.sig uses a closed EhdrMachine enum (~5604, members AARCH64/LOONGARCH/PPC64/RISCV/SPARCV9/X86_64) so its relocation switches can be exhaustive; adding BPF breaks every switch until handled (the design lists the MachineRelocType family lines ~943-1177 and targetPageAlign ~5658, but exploration found MORE ehdrMachine() switch sites around 5692/5743/5764/5776/6444/6888/7851/8327/8726/8742/8776/8785/8791/8983/9039/10759/10919 — build until clean, do not trust the list alone).
directory_structure: lib/std/ = the standard library + Target/CPU/ELF definitions the compiler links against (Target.sig, Target/bpf.sig, elf.sig). src/ = the compiler itself (main.sig driver, target.sig capability predicates, Compilation.sig + Compilation/Config.sig link/compile-option resolution, codegen/llvm.sig LLVM lowering, link/Elf2.sig self-hosted ELF linker and link/Lld.sig the vendored-LLD wrapper which sBPF must bypass). compiler/ = ABI/target docs (SB0_ABI_TARGET.md; add SBPF_SOLANA_TARGET.md). tools/ = build drivers and generators (add build-sbpf.ps1). .build/sbpf-test/ = throwaway test modules. .agents/tasks/sbpf-solana/ = design, review, plan, and these FEAT artifacts.
